question.problem:
Which of the following congruences have *precisely four* solutions modulo $20?$

I. $4x≡9\,(\text{mod}\,20)$

II. $12x≡16\,(\text{mod}\,20)$

III. $8x≡12\,(\text{mod}\,20)$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14269988/assets/b65fc4830e0b060d62226b41d5ccb7bdc63d0ad594f7a42a2628597409bba3af.png)

      

Recall the following facts regarding the congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n):$

- The congruence has no solutions modulo $n$ if and only if 

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)\,\text{⧸}|\,b.
$$

- The congruence has $\text{gcd}(a,n)$ solutions modulo $n$ if and only if 

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)\,|\,b.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our congruences.

- Congruence I has no solutions. We have $a=4$ and $n=20$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(4,20)=4.
$$

Since $b=9$ is not divisible by $4,$ this congruence has no solutions.

- Congruence II has four solutions modulo $20.$ We have $a=12$ and $n=20$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(12,20)=4.
$$

Since $b=16$ is divisible by $4,$ this congruence has $4$ solutions.

- Congruence III has four solutions modulo $20.$ We have $a=8$ and $n=20$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(8,20)=4.
$$

Since $b=12$ is divisible by $4,$ this congruence has $4$ solutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only".
